Elena — thanks for the heads up and the summary. We saw the same auth spike in our telemetry and have begun a short triage. High level:

1) Immediate status: we saw ~27 failed token exchanges followed by 3 successful exchanges tied to 2 service accounts in your tenant. No lateral activity detected in application logs in the 30m after the events.

2) Actions we've kicked off:
- Rotated the affected service account keys and revoked active tokens (containment).
- Created a sanitized telemetry export scoped to 2026-05-18T08:15:00-2026-05-18T09:00:00 PDT for delivery.
- Opened an internal investigation and preserved raw logs for forensics (s3 retention + internal KMS audit).

3) IRP summary (short):
- Triage & scope (identify impacted principals, isolate credentials)
- Containment (revoke tokens, rotate keys, block suspicious IPs)
- Collection (preserve raw telemetry, checksum & chain-of-custody)
- Analysis (forensic timelines, correlate with vendor logs)
- Communication (notify customers, share sanitized artifacts for compliance)

I am looping in Neha (SOC 2 / compliance) to own delivery of the SIG/CAIQ artifacts and the telemetry extracts. Neha — can your team prepare:
- A sanitized telemetry export (auth logs + token exchange attempts)
- KMS access audit (events tied to the service account IDs)
- A brief postmortem note once triage completes (1–2 pages)

We can deliver via SecureSys' upload link or upload to our encrypted transfer bucket and share an expiring link. ETA for the initial sanitized package: today EOD PDT.

Elena — follow-up and closure note. Thank you for your patience. We delivered the sanitized package to the SecureSys uploader at 2026-05-18T18:02:14 PDT. Package contents (sanitized):
- auth-incident-timeline.csv (included)
- redwood-telemetry-sample-ids.jsonl (included)
- ksm-access-logs.tar.gz (included)
- brief-postmortem.pdf (2 pages; timeline, root cause, remediation)

Postmortem highlights (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a misconfigured long-lived service account credential that was accessible from an external CI job belonging to GoldenCorp; attacker/automation used rotated credentials to exchange tokens.
- Impact: limited to 3 token exchanges tied to two service accounts; access was limited to authentication endpoints — no data-plane access was observed.
- Mitigation: immediate key rotation, token revocation, and temporary IP blocklist; added an automated alert rule for anomalous token exchange rates per tenant.
- Next steps: recommend rotating any long-lived credentials in GoldenCorp CI, adopt short-lived service account patterns, and enable per-tenant token exchange rate alerts (we can help with a runbook).

Related artifacts and links:
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4123 (investigation)
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/56789 (customer record)
